transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Alex (Maple Eng Mgr), Samira (SRE), Liam (Product), Ruth (Security)

Summary (auto): go/no-go prep, canary values, runbooks assigned, security follow-up.

[00:00] Maya: okay everyone thanks for joining on time, I think we have about 45 minutes so we'll go through the telemetry, then the A/B plan and finally runbooks and security asks. quick roll call?
[00:12] Alex: Alex here.
[00:13] Samira: Samira, SRE.
[00:15] Liam: Liam, product.
[00:17] Ruth: Ruth on security.
[00:19] Maya: great, Maya, Diego and Priya from Redwood.

[00:30] Maya: real quick first, did everyone get the dashboard link I sent this morning? the live one with p50/p95/p99 and the semantic-quality eval?
[00:38] Samira: yes I pulled it up, though the p95 spikes at 200ms mark on Tuesday were surprising - we thought the batching would smooth that out.
[00:46] Diego: right, so let me explain -- the workload shifted to longer sequences and the runtime proactively increased batch size which pushed one of the workers into a slower kernel path. that can bump p95. it's a tradeoff batch sizing does to save tokens but occasionally increases tail latency.
[01:05] Samira: okay makes sense, can we pin batch size for the canary? we want consistent latency for user-facing flow.
[01:12] Diego: yes, in the pilot config we can set maxBatchSize and a jitter window; for canary we'll recommend capping at 8 to keep p95 under 180ms based on the replay tests.
[01:22] Alex: what about KV cache warmup? I think a lot of the spike correlated with cold KV misses.
[01:27] Diego: good catch. the warmup script we've shown before will pre-populate prefixes for the first N users; I'll share an adapted script today. warmup plus smaller batches should stabilize the tail.

[01:40] Liam: on A/B, product wants to measure not just latency but semantic quality delta. are we able to capture eval metrics for A/B?
[01:48] Maya: yes, Redwood Optimize can run eval sets against each variant and surface regression alerts. we'll tie the canary to both latency and a small prompt-set quality SLO.
[01:57] Liam: what's the noise floor on that? I don't want false positives on minor wording changes.
[02:02] Priya: for POC we recommend threshold at 2% BLEU-ish equivalent or whichever ranking metric you prefer; we can show delta over the sample and set a rolling window.
[02:10] Liam: okay good.

[02:18] Ruth: from security, quick question: if we fallback to dedicated nodes where is the data routed and how is keys handled? we need KMS/HSM in path and audit logs.
[02:27] Maya: fallback preserves the same VPC egress rules; the dedicated pool can be provisioned in your VPC and Redwood supports customer-managed KMS. we'll send an architecture note.
[02:36] Ruth: and logs? we need tamper-evident audit trails for request metadata retention for 90 days.
[02:40] Priya: audit logs can be shipped to your Splunk/CloudWatch. the private deployment path includes immutable log sinks; we'll include the retention options.

[02:52] Alex: timeline question: we're aiming for cutover the week of 12/21 pending results. is that still realistic?
[02:58] Maya: yes if the staging ramps are clean. proposed schedule: this week run two staging ramps 10% then 50% traffic, next week full go-decision meeting and a short production dry-run in a quiet window.
[03:11] Samira: what's the quiet window length?
[03:13] Diego: typically 2 hours, with a 30 minute observation at 50% then increase to 100% if metrics hold for 30 minutes. we also want to validate error budgets and automatic rollback triggers.
[03:25] Samira: ok. automatic rollback triggers - what exact signals?
[03:28] Maya: error rate > 0.5% absolute increase or p95 latency > +40% baseline for 3 consecutive minutes would trigger an automated rollback to previous pool. also semantic-quality alert will be manual but flagged.
[03:44] Liam: for A/B do we standardize the bucketing key? we want deterministic splits by user id.
[03:49] Diego: yes we recommend user-id hashing with a shard salt; Redwood's router supports sticky assignment for sessions to avoid cross-variant drift.

[04:00] Maya: Diego, can you talk about cost delta for hybrid fallback - customers often ask what the worst-case monthly expense looks like.
[04:07] Diego: short answer, dedicated pool hourly + token cost. for your observed throughput the delta is roughly +18% at peak if both pools are active; but most of the time fallback is only a small tail. I'll put numbers in a spreadsheet.
[04:19] Alex: please include a scenario where we run 10% of traffic on dedicated continuously for warm cache.
[04:24] Diego: will do.

[04:30] Maya: runbook owners - Samira you'll own the staged traffic execution, Diego/Redwood will run the warmup and instrument traces, Ruth owns security signoff, Alex and Liam will own product acceptance criteria.
[04:41] Samira: yes that works.

[04:46] Ruth: one more security nit: retention of prompts. we need an option to redact PII and exclude prompt storage in logs. can Redwood support redaction at ingest?
[04:54] Priya: yes, we have redaction hooks and policy-based retention. will include recommended config.

[05:00] Maya: any blockers left?
[05:03] Alex: none other than getting the staging results in time.
[05:05] Samira: we will run the two ramps Wednesday and Friday in staging.
[05:09] Maya: perfect, we'll follow up with the canary thresholds doc and runbook.

[05:15] Diego: quick note - for the warmup script we'll show two variants: a prepopulate-only and a streaming warmup that runs gradually to avoid thundering herd. choose the streaming one if you expect steady traffic spikes.
[05:29] Samira: streaming sounds safer.
[05:31] Liam: question about experiment metrics - do you surface likelihood calibration or just top-1 accuracy?
[05:36] Maya: we can surface multiple metrics: top-1, reranker agreement, BLEU-style overlap and a custom rubric from your product team.
[05:43] Liam: great.

[05:47] Maya: ok last bit: expectations for the dry-run in production - we'll need a quiet window and a set of canary prompts to verify semantic parity. Diego can you draft the prompt set template?
[05:56] Diego: yes I'll attach the template with seed prompts and expected buckets.
[06:00] Ruth: timeline recap?
[06:02] Maya: recap - Diego uploads warmup script and runbook (due 12/09), Maya shares canary thresholds and pricing delta (due 12/10), Samira runs staging ramps and posts telemetry (due 12/15), Ruth sends security KMS decision (due 12/14). we'll reconvene after ramps for go/no-go.
[06:22] Alex: thanks everyone.
[06:24] Maya: thanks all, end of meeting.

Note: occasional transcript errors present (names and product terms sometimes misrecognized).
